0.name: Values Log
0.description:
You can challenge a Value Statement (act against your own Value) when you have the spotlight:

  • Roll three dice for that Value instead of one
  • Step the Value down

At the end of the session either rewrite the Value Statement and recover the dice, or keep the new Value dice and:

  • Step up another Value.
  • Record the act you took against the Value you just stepped up in the Value Log.

If you step up a Value beyond a D12 you must read to the table the Value Log.  The other players will then vote regarding how you transcend that Value.

1.name: Session Log
1.description:
Record key events from a session, one session per section.

  • Callback: reference a previously recorded session during play as you act as an in-character nod to the past.  Gain a benfit equal to anything a Plot Point could bye (byt do not gain a Plot Point).  Each past session can only be called back once per session.
  • Training Up: Spend recorded sessions to make improvements to your character.  Once a session has been used for training up it can no longer be used as a Callback.
Improvement Cost
Turn a scene Asset into a Signature Asset 1 session
Switch out a Distinction for a new one 1 session
Step up a Signature Asset 2 sessions
Unlock a new SFX 2 sessions
Step up a Kill 3 sessions

3.name: Limits & SFX
3.description: To the Akashics, magick is the perfection of the self. The universe is an illusion; by mastering their own physical and mental discipline (Do), they force the universe to align with their internal harmony.

0.label: Limit - Broken Flow
0.value:
Decline Paradox stress ≤ your rolled Power die: take a plot point, shut down the set.

Recovery: recovers when you regain your centre at a scene of meditation.

1.label: SFX - Perfected Kata
1.value: Step up an Akashic Power trait when engaging in continuous, uninterrupted motion or meditation. This lasts until you choose to end Perfected Kata or until the end of the scene, whichever comes first. If you take a complication that breaks your physical stance or concentration, lose this benefit and additionally step down the selected Power trait until you recover the complication.

2.label: SFX - Still Mind
2.value: When you roll a Hitch while acting from perfect focus, spend a plot point to reroll your dice pool and keep the new result (this cannot rescue a vulgar botch).

3.name: Limit & SFX

0.label: Limit - Divine Silence
0.value:
Decline Paradox stress ≤ your rolled Power die: take a plot point, shut down the set. If your working was entirely selfish, the One does not intervene and this Limit is unavailable.

Recovery: recovers no earlier than the next scene, when you raise your voice in genuine faith, in prayer, hymn, or invocation in good conscience.

1.label: SFX - Divine Invocation
1.value: Step up a Chorus Power trait for the rest of the scene when vocally singing, chanting, or praying aloud. While Divine Invocation is in effect, if you use any Power trait in silence or for selfish ends, immediately take a Crisis of Faith d6 complication each time.

2.label: SFX - Choir Eternal
2.value: When you cast aloud in concert with allies, keep an additional effect die and grant it to an ally as an Asset.

3.description: The universe is a shattered melody, and magick is the act of singing the divine frequencies back into perfect harmony. They manipulate the raw, underlying light of creation.

3.name: Limit & SFX

0.label: Limit - The Comedown
0.value:
Decline Paradox stress ≤ your rolled Power die but do not shut down the set. Instead, the backlash crashes into your nervous system. Take an Exhaustion complication one step larger than the Paradox avoided.

Recovery: the Exhaustion complication recovers when the pulse returns, the next time you reach an altered or heightened state. When that happens, replace Exhaustion with an Intoxicated complication of equal rating for the rest of the scene. The Intoxicated complication resolves at the end of the scene.

1.label: SFX - Chase the Dragon
1.value: Step up a Cult Power trait for the rest of the scene when you engage in a vice, intense exertion, or extreme sensory input. In exchange, step down all Skills for the rest of the scene from intoxication, exhaustion, or sensory distortion.

2.label: SFX - Too Far Gone
2.value: When your pursuit of sensation blinds you to a danger, gain a plot point; the GM steps up a complication against you by one.

3.description: The Cult pushes their bodies past sensory limits to perceive the Lakashim (the divine pulse), treating time and perception as fluid boundaries to be dissolved.

3.name: Limit & SFX
3.description: Reality is a negotiation. Every object, storm, and location has an awake, aware spirit. Magick is the act of stepping sideways, bargaining with, or commanding these entities.

0.label: Limit - Spirit Debt
0.value:
Decline Paradox stress ≤ your rolled Power die but do not shut down the set. Instead, the rejected Paradox angers the local spirits. Create an Offended Spirits Paradox Flaw complication one step larger than the Paradox avoided.

Recovery: in addition to the usual ways of clearing a Paradox Flaw, the Offended Spirits Paradox Flaw also resolves when you renew your standing with the spirits by means of an offering, a rite, or a kept pact.

1.label: SFX - Shaman's Bargain
1.value: Step up a Dreamspeaker Power trait for the rest of the scene when you make a promise and an offering to the spirits. The offering can be a physical sacrifice, burned tobacco or incense, or your own spilled blood. If you break a pact you have sworn to a spirit, you lose this benefit and the GM may immediately inflict a Spirit’s Rebuke d6 complication on you.

2.label: SFX - Counsel of Spirits
2.value: Spend a plot point to consult a local spirit, giving yourself or an ally a d8 Asset for a single test, contest, or challenge.

3.name: Limit & SFX
3.description: Magick is the art of endings. They follow the currents of karma, steer the hand of fate, and prune the dead branches of reality so that the Wheel of Ages may continue its eternal turning.

0.label: Limit - Weight of Jhor
0.value:
Decline Paradox stress ≤ your rolled Power die but do not shut down the set. You internalise the necrotic decay. Take a Jhor (death taint) complication equal to the Paradox avoided. Jhor will oppose any action the mage takes that does not further their study or knowledge of death. The higher the rating, the more pallid and death-like the mage appears. Jhor can only be reduced by the recovery condition.

Recovery: the Jhor complication steps down when the Wheel turns again, the next time you let something end that must end, releasing the dark energy.

1.label: SFX - The Good Death
1.value: Step up a Euthanatos Power trait for the rest of the scene if you take decisive action to permanently end a corrupted, stagnant, or dangerous threat. Step down a Euthanatos Power trait for the rest of the scene if you hesitate out of mercy or compromise.

2.label: SFX - Fate Foretold
2.value: When you Read the Karma of a target and assess their fate before you act, gain a d8 Asset you can use against them for the scene.

3.name: Limit & SFX
3.description: The Order views the universe as a rigid machine subject to magickal laws. Magick is an uncompromising science of vocabulary and willpower, a verb done unto a noun, spoken aloud with the proper tools in the proper ritual.

0.label: Limit - Flawed Formula
0.value:
Decline Paradox stress ≤ the higher of your two rolled Power dice: take a plot point, shut down both sets.

Recovery: recovers when you have tools, voice, and time together again, in a proper casting environment.

1.label: SFX - Formulaic Rigidity
1.value: Combine one Verb and one Noun trait to shape your effect, rolling an extra die. However, step down the highest die in your pool if you lack your proper focal items (wands, seals, pentacles), cannot speak your incantations aloud, or lack the time to execute the ritual geometry.

2.label: SFX - Prepared Formula
2.value: Spend a plot point to declare you have a rote prepared for exactly this situation, creating a d8 Asset for the test, contest, or challenge.

0.label: Limit - Ping Spike

3.name: Limit & SFX
3.description: The ultimate scavengers of the magickal world. They survive by stitching together the discarded scraps of the other Traditions into a postmodern, romanticised pastiche.

0.label: Limit - Reality Bites
0.value:
Decline Paradox stress ≤ your rolled Power die: shut down the set. You may immediately step up a mundane Skill for the rest of the scene as you rely purely on street smarts.

Recovery: recovers no earlier than the next scene, when you are free to spend time with people who really understand you.

1.label: SFX - Postmodern Pastiche
1.value: Step up a Hollow One Power trait for the rest of the scene when you work magick through pure style and attitude, treating the rite as performance, irony, or aesthetic rather than sincere belief. Step down all Power traits for the rest of the scene if you use the stepped-up trait while treating magick with solemn, earnest reverence.

2.label: SFX - Magpie's Hoard
2.value: Spend a plot point to use any one Tradition Power trait you have witnessed in play this session at a d6, justified by your scavenging.
